basic_identification.full_title: Miner's Safety Goggles — Specification (खनिकों के लिये सुरक्षा चश्मे — विशिष्टि)
basic_identification.sector_category: Heavy Mechanical Engineering / Mining (finalized by the Mines Sectional Committee, HMD 05, of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This Indian Standard prescribes the material specifications, design configurations, dimensions, safety requirements, and testing protocols for safety goggles used by miners to protect eyes against hazards such as mechanical impact from flying rock chips and fine dust particles encountered during mining operations.

version_status_and_amendments.supersedes: None (Developed as a dedicated personal protective equipment standard specifically optimized for the mining sector's harsh mechanical and environmental conditions)

allied_standards.title: Code of Practice on Occupational Safety and Health Audit
allied_standards.relevance: Personal protective equipment (PPE) compliance is a primary gate in mine safety audits. Under IS 14489, mine safety inspectors check on-site drilling, cutting, and roof-bolting crews to verify they are equipped with and actively wearing safety goggles conforming to IS 14352.

allied_standards.title: Occupational Health and Safety Management System
allied_standards.relevance: Unifies operational risk mitigation, requiring daily safety logs, chemical detector checks, and machinery guard validation.

allied_standards.title: Code of Practice for General Steel Construction
allied_standards.relevance: The master structural steel construction code in India, regulating steel headframes, gantry supports, and mining structures where welding and cutting generate sparks and slag requiring eye protection.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Specification (Heavy Mechanical Engineering Department / Mining)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Product Specification. Manufacturers are highly encouraged to apply for a BIS license to print the physical ISI 'Standard Mark' directly on the packaging of miner's safety goggles or the component itself to certify material quality and safety compliance in the mining market.

requirements.detail: Observed or calculated final test values, observed dimensions, or physical properties must be rounded off mathematically in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.
The goggle frame must be of sound construction and made of durable plastic or other suitable materials capable of resisting mechanical impacts and prolonged moisture exposure.
The head-band material must be sweat-resistant, non-irritant, and shall not cause skin disease under prolonged shifts.

Lenses must be fabricated from plastic materials, toughened or laminated glass, or a combination of these materials. Untreated glass is strictly prohibited unless backed by plastic or laminated glass to prevent shattering.

Goggles required for use in underground mines shall have no metal parts made of aluminium, magnesium, titanium, or their alloys to prevent light-metal frictional sparking in explosive methane or coal dust atmospheres.

Goggles are classified into Type A (Cup-type, with two eye-pieces connected across the nose with adjustment arrangements) and Type B (Box-type, providing total enclosure of both eyes with either separate lens holders or a single continuous window lens).
Lenses for Type A goggles must be circular with a nominal diameter of 50 ± 2 mm.
Type B goggles fitted with separate lens holders must have circular lenses of 50 ± 2 mm in diameter.

Type B goggles fitted with a single-piece window lens must feature two symmetrically spaced circular viewing fields, each with a minimum diameter of 52 mm, with their centers spaced exactly 62 mm apart measured horizontally in the front plane as worn.
The head-band must have a minimum width of 10 mm to distribute pressure evenly and prevent slipping.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 14352 : 1996 (Reaffirmed 2022) is the primary national Indian Standard specification prescribing construction, dimensional, material, and safety requirements for miner's safety goggles. Developed under the Mines Sectional Committee (HMD 05), the standard unifies eye protection specs for the hazardous mining sector. It classifies goggles into Cup-type (Type A) and Box-type (Type B) configurations with standard 50 mm circular lens sizes, enforces sweat-resistant head-bands and shatter-resistant lenses (polycarbonate, toughened, or laminated glass), and mandates a critical underground safety rule: no light-metal parts (aluminum, magnesium, or titanium) are permitted to prevent frictional sparking in explosive coal mine atmospheres.
